leaf.format: <tag> NUL <logFormatVersion> NUL <canonical JSON of { envelope, signature }>

checkpoint.format: <tag> NUL <version> NUL <canonical JSON of the checkpoint>

hashing.construction: RFC 6962 section 2.1 / RFC 9162 section 2.1 — a reuse of the published construction, not a claim of CT protocol compliance

howTheseWereProduced.keys: One ephemeral NIST P-256 evidence-signing key pair generated once; it signs both the seals and the checkpoints, as the product does. The private half was never written anywhere and no longer exists.
howTheseWereProduced.immutability: evidence-log/v1/ is immutable exactly like a released schema directory, commitment/v1/ and trust-registry/v1/. ECDSA is randomized, so regenerating would produce different signatures; these are the published bytes and they are what both runtimes must agree on.
howTheseWereProduced.twoLayers: The deterministic material (leaf hashes, tree heads, proofs) must be reproduced byte for byte by any runtime. The signed material must be accepted or refused identically, with the same reason code.
howTheseWereProduced.identifiers: Every identifier is synthetic. No real tenant, action or payload identifier appears in these vectors, and a checkpoint carries none by construction.

verificationRequirement: treeSize and rootHash are one inseparable pair taken from one signed checkpoint; a verifier never accepts either from the prover. See docs/EVIDENCE-LOG.md section 6.

rfc6962KnownAnswers.note: The published Certificate Transparency test tree: leaf data as hex, hashed and composed by this format. Proves both runtimes compute the published construction, not a lookalike.

canonical.note: The canonical JSON of seal-1 and of checkpoint-1, i.e. each signing/leaf input with its NUL-separated header removed — the readable anchors. Every other value is pinned by hash, and a hash match is a byte match.

acceptanceChain.note: Accepted in order by a verifier that holds state; growth between accepted checkpoints is connected by a consistency proof. Re-presenting the already accepted checkpoint is idempotent.

refusals.description: a checkpoint declaring a format version this implementation does not speak
the checkpoint member set is closed
rootHash must name its suite: "sha256:" then 64 lowercase hex digits
issuedAt must be a canonical UTC timestamp
a leaf holds exactly envelope and signature
a leaf carries an envelope of version 1
a leaf signature must be unpadded base64url
an ES256 signature is exactly 64 bytes
the checkpointed record was mutated afterwards: its commitment digest changed, so its leaf hash changed, and the original proof no longer leads to any checkpointed root
the right leaf presented at the wrong position
a tree size that does not match the signed checkpoint pair (treeSize, rootHash)
a proof path with a node removed
a proof path with two nodes exchanged
a leaf index that does not exist in a tree of this size
a checkpointed leaf was deleted; no proof connects the old head to the new one
a leaf was inserted before the checkpointed boundary
two checkpointed leaves were exchanged
a smaller tree cannot extend a larger one
two heads at one size that disagree
a well-formed checkpoint whose treeSize was altered after signing
a correct checkpoint with one signature character altered
a signature that is not unpadded base64url
a key that is not a valid public JWK
an old checkpoint presented as current after a newer one was accepted
two correctly signed checkpoints with the same sequence and different heads
a later checkpoint at the same tree size naming a different head
a later checkpoint covering fewer leaves — the log shrank
a checkpoint from a different log entirely
growth asserted without a consistency proof is refused, not believed
